Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image show any change to the mug’s position relative to the headphones?
node.criteria: pass: The mug’s position relative to the headphones visibly changed. fail: The mug’s position relative to the headphones visibly did not change. unknown: A change cannot be determined from the available images.
node.binding: Compare the original and edited images only to assess progress toward the requested relative-position change; unrelated edits do not count.

node_traces.evidence: The mug’s position relative to the headphones visibly changed between the source and edited images; the edited image shows a mug on the headphones’ right, indicating progress toward the requested move.

fulfillment: The node overweights the final-state relation and treats any positional change as progress. In the edited image, the original blue mug appears as a blurred remnant on the left, while two small mug-like objects are visible; the headphones are also altered. The trace does not establish which object is the original target or whether the requested mug was moved, and its claim that the mug is right of the headphones conflicts with the visible arrangement/identity ambiguity. Bind the target and reference to the same objects across source and edit, and require evidence of the requested target’s movement plus its final relation before calling completion. Distinguish established partial progress from unresolved identity or visual evidence; do not infer progress merely from a change or let supporting observations independently earn completion. The high-confidence ‘yes’ despite these ambiguities suggests the criterion/evidence aggregation needs calibration. No transport or schema failure is indicated.

Keep progress distinct from completion: this support check may establish a genuine movement even if the final relation is not achieved, but should not infer movement from a mug merely appearing on the right. The trace does not resolve which mug, if any, is the original target, so this evidence warrants uncertainty rather than a high-confidence pass.
